learn.name: Claude Managed Agents API
learn.oneLineDescription: Hosted agent harness: define config, spin up sandbox, stream results — no infra.

detail.whatItDoes:
Claude Managed Agents is Anthropic's hosted infrastructure for running autonomous Claude agents. You define a versioned Agent config (model, system prompt, tools, MCP servers), create an Environment (cloud or self-hosted), and start Sessions. Each session gets an isolated container with bash, file ops, web search, and code execution built in. The agent loop, context compaction, prompt caching, and session state are all managed on Anthropic's side.

Pricing is $0.08/session-hour billed to the millisecond (idle time does not count) plus standard Claude token costs. Multi-agent orchestration, webhooks, MCP vault credentials, and self-hosted sandboxes (run tool execution on your own infra via Cloudflare, Modal, Vercel, or Daytona) are all now in public beta under the `managed-agents-2026-04-01` beta header.
detail.whoItsFor: Backend engineers who want to ship autonomous agent pipelines — PR review bots, CI code-quality agents, documentation generators, overnight test runners — without building sandbox infrastructure, managing Docker containers, or writing their own agent loop. Also useful for teams already using Claude Code interactively who want to schedule or automate the same work programmatically.
pros: No DIY orchestration: agent loop, context compaction, retries, and sandbox are all handled by Anthropic
Session state is durable — sessions survive harness crashes and resume cleanly
Self-hosted sandbox option lets you move tool execution to your own infra for compliance requirements
Versioned Agent configs enable GitOps-style rollout and rollback without breaking running sessions
All Anthropic API accounts have access with no waitlist
cons: Claude-only — no multi-model routing; for GPT or open-weight models you need your own orchestration
Not eligible for Zero Data Retention or HIPAA BAA coverage because sessions are stateful server-side
Multi-agent orchestration and dreaming (agent memory consolidation) are still research preview, gated access
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Anthropic API key with an active billing account (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`)
- `ant` CLI or the Python/TypeScript SDK
- All Managed Agents requests need the beta header `managed-agents-2026-04-01` (SDKs set it automatically)

## 1. Install the `ant` CLI

```bash
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install anthropics/tap/ant

# Verify
ant --version

# Set your API key
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."
```

## 2. Create an Agent config

```bash
ant beta:agents create \
  --name "code-reviewer" \
  --model '{id: claude-opus-4-8}' \
  --system "You are a senior code reviewer. Analyze repos for bugs, security issues, and style. Be specific about line numbers." \
  --tool '{type: agent_toolset_20260401}'
# Save the returned agent_id, e.g. agent_abc123
```

The `agent_toolset_20260401` tool type enables bash, file read/write, web search, web fetch, grep, and glob — all sandboxed.

## 3. Create an Environment

```bash
ant beta:environments create \
  --name "python-dev" \
  --config '{type: cloud, networking: {type: unrestricted}, packages: {pip: ["pytest", "black", "ruff"]}}'
# Save the returned environment_id, e.g. env_xyz789
```

## 4. Start a Session and send a task

```bash
# Start session
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/sessions \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"agent_id": "agent_abc123", "environment_id": "env_xyz789"}'
# Save session_id from response

# Send a task
curl https://api.anthropic.com/v1/sessions/sess_123/events \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"type": "user_message", "content": "Clone https://github.com/myorg/api-service, run the test suite, and give me a code quality report."}'
```

## 5. Stream results

```bash
curl -N https://api.anthropic.com/v1/sessions/sess_123/events/stream \
  -H "x-api-key: $ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" \
  -H "anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01"
```

## Python SDK (alternative)

```python
pip install anthropic
```

```python
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

# SDKs auto-set the managed-agents-2026-04-01 beta header
agent = client.beta.agents.create(
    name="code-reviewer",
    model="claude-opus-4-8",
    system_prompt="You are a senior code reviewer.",
    tools=[{"type": "agent_toolset_20260401"}],
)

env = client.beta.environments.create(
    name="python-dev",
    config={"type": "cloud", "networking": {"type": "unrestricted"}},
)

session = client.beta.sessions.create(
    agent_id=agent.id,
    environment_id=env.id,
)

for event in client.beta.sessions.stream(session.id, message="Review the latest commit for security issues"):
    print(event)
```

## Gotchas
- **Beta header is mandatory** — raw HTTP calls will 400 without `anthropic-beta: managed-agents-2026-04-01`
- **Do not store credentials in system prompts** — use the vault system (`client.beta.vaults.credentials.create`) and pass `vault_ids` at session creation
- **SSE stream has no replay** — if your stream drops mid-tool-call, reconnect with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/events`, dedupe by event ID, then reopen the stream; otherwise the session deadlocks
- **Not HIPAA-eligible** — sessions are stateful server-side; not covered by ZDR or BAA

learn.name: Gemini CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Free, open-source terminal AI agent backed by Gemini — 1M token context, MCP support.

detail.whatItDoes:
Gemini CLI is Google's open-source (Apache 2.0) terminal AI agent. It runs a ReAct loop against Gemini models with built-in tools: bash execution, file read/write, web search, and MCP server integration. It supports GEMINI.md context files (same idea as CLAUDE.md), session checkpointing so long coding runs survive crashes, headless/scripting mode for CI pipelines, and a skills system for shareable capability packs.

The free tier with a personal Google account gives 60 requests/minute and 1,000 requests/day — no API key needed. For heavier workloads, pass a Google AI Studio or Vertex AI key. Note: Google announced at I/O 2026 that Antigravity 2.0 (a Go-based CLI) is the longer-term direction; Gemini CLI has a sunset date of June 18, 2026 for free/individual users, after which Antigravity CLI is the migration path. Existing Google AI Studio or Vertex API-key users can continue past that date.
detail.whoItsFor: Budget-conscious developers who want a Claude Code or Codex CLI equivalent at zero cost. Google Cloud teams that want native GCP service integration. Open-source advocates who want to inspect and extend the agent. Anyone building CI automation who needs a free headless coding agent that can pipe from stdin.
pros: Genuinely free for personal use — 60 req/min, 1,000 req/day with a Google account, no card required
1M token context window handles large codebases without chunking
MCP server support lets you extend with GitHub, Slack, databases, and custom tools via settings.json
Session checkpointing survives crashes; headless mode works in GitHub Actions and cron jobs
Apache 2.0 licensed — fully auditable and forkable
cons: Sunset for free/individual users on June 18, 2026 — migration to Antigravity CLI required after that date
Requires Node.js 20+ runtime (not a single binary like some alternatives)
Free tier rate limits (60 req/min) can throttle long agentic loops on large codebases
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node.js 20 or later (`node --version` to check)
- A Google account (no credit card needed for free tier)
- macOS 15+, Windows 11 24H2+, or Ubuntu 20.04+

## Install

```bash
# Stable channel (released every Tuesday 20:00 UTC)
npm install -g @google/gemini-cli

# Verify
gemini --version

# Alternative: Homebrew (macOS)
brew install google-gemini/gemini-cli/gemini-cli
```

## Authenticate

```bash
# Option A: Personal Google account (free tier, no API key needed)
gemini login
# Opens browser — sign in with Google account

# Option B: API key (AI Studio or Vertex for higher limits)
export GEMINI_API_KEY="your-ai-studio-key"
# Or for Vertex:
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="your-project-id"
gcloud auth application-default login
```

## First session

```bash
# Start interactive session in your project root
cd your-project
gemini

# Inside the session:
> Give me a summary of all changes merged to main this week
> Write unit tests for src/auth.ts and run them
> Fix the failing test in src/utils.test.ts
```

## Headless mode (CI / scripts)

```bash
# Single-shot prompt from CLI
gemini --headless -p "Review this PR diff for security issues" < pr.diff

# In a GitHub Actions step:
- name: Security review
  run: echo "$(git diff main)" | gemini --headless -p "Flag any security issues in this diff"
  env:
    GEMINI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GEMINI_API_KEY }}
```

## Add an MCP server (e.g. GitHub)

```bash
gemini mcp add github \
  --command "npx" \
  --args "-y,@modelcontextprotocol/server-github" \
  --env GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN=ghp_yourtoken

# Verify
gemini mcp list

# Use in session
gemini
> @github List my open pull requests
```

## GEMINI.md context file

Create a `GEMINI.md` in your project root to give the agent persistent context:

```markdown
# Project: Payments API
- Language: TypeScript, Node 22
- Test runner: Vitest (`npm test`)
- Lint: `npm run lint` (ESLint + Prettier)
- Never edit files in `dist/` — that is build output
- Open PRs against `main`; squash merge only
```

## Gotchas
- **Sunset June 18, 2026** — free/individual users must migrate to Antigravity CLI after this date; API-key users can continue
- **MCP server cold start** — if `gemini mcp list` stalls, your MCP server is taking too long to start via `npx`; add `--timeout 5000` to `mcp add` or remove unused servers
- **Node deprecation warning on install** — a transitive native addon prints a deprecation notice; it is cosmetic and the install succeeds
- **`GEMINI_API_KEY` vs `gcloud` auth** — set one, not both; having both configured can cause silent auth failures

learn.name: ant CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: kubectl-style CLI for Anthropic's Claude API — manages agents, environments, and sessions.

detail.whatItDoes:
The `ant` CLI is Anthropic's official Go-based command-line client for the Claude API, launched April 2026 alongside Claude Managed Agents. It exposes every Claude API resource as a shell subcommand with a `kubectl`-style resource/verb structure (`ant [resource] <command> [flags]`). It handles YAML-based agent config files for GitOps workflows, auto-paginates list endpoints, auto-injects the correct `anthropic-beta` headers so you never have to track them manually, and supports `@path` syntax to inline file contents into any string field.

Beta resources — agents, sessions, environments, deployments, skills, vaults, memory stores — live under the `beta:` prefix. For programmatic agent execution inside applications, pair `ant` with the Python or TypeScript SDK; `ant` is the control-plane tool, the SDK is the data-plane tool.
detail.whoItsFor: DevOps and platform engineers who manage Claude agent infrastructure via CI/CD pipelines. Developers who want to provision, debug, and rotate agent configs from the terminal without writing curl commands or maintaining JSON request bodies. Teams doing GitOps-style agent config management (check YAML into git, deploy from CI).
pros: Auto-sets the correct anthropic-beta header for every beta endpoint — no header tracking needed
YAML agent config files enable GitOps: check configs into git, apply from CI, roll back to previous versions
Tab completion for bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell speeds up working with the long beta: namespaced commands
Go binary — single installable with no Node or Python runtime dependency
cons: Requires a paid Anthropic API account — no free tier for Managed Agents
All Managed Agents commands are under the beta: prefix; command structure may change before GA
Not the right tool for embedding agent interactions in applications — use the Python/TypeScript SDK for that
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Anthropic API key (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) — generate at console.anthropic.com
- macOS, Linux, or Windows (Go binary, no Node/Python required)

## Install

```bash
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install anthropics/tap/ant

# Linux (direct binary)
curl -sSL https://api.anthropic.com/cli/install.sh | sh

# Verify
ant --version
```

## Authenticate

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."

# Optional: shell completion (zsh)
ant completion zsh > ~/.zfunc/_ant
echo 'fpath=(~/.zfunc $fpath)' >> ~/.zshrc
echo 'autoload -Uz compinit && compinit' >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc
```

## Create and deploy an agent (imperative style)

```bash
# Create an agent config
ant beta:agents create \
  --name "pr-reviewer" \
  --model '{id: claude-opus-4-8}' \
  --system "You are a senior code reviewer. Clone repos, run tests, report bugs with line numbers." \
  --tool '{type: agent_toolset_20260401}'
# Note the returned agent_id

# Create a cloud environment
ant beta:environments create \
  --name "python-ci" \
  --config '{type: cloud, networking: {type: unrestricted}, packages: {pip: ["pytest", "ruff"]}}'
# Note the returned environment_id

# Start a session
ant beta:sessions create \
  --agent-id agent_abc123 \
  --environment-id env_xyz789
# Note the returned session_id

# Send a task
ant beta:sessions messages create sess_123 \
  --content "Review the latest commit on main for security vulnerabilities"

# Stream results
ant beta:sessions stream sess_123
```

## GitOps style (YAML config)

```yaml
# agent.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Agent
name: pr-reviewer
model:
  id: claude-opus-4-8
system: |
  You are a senior code reviewer.
  Always check for SQL injection, SSRF, and insecure deserialization.
tools:
  - type: agent_toolset_20260401
mcp_servers:
  - name: github
    url: https://mcp.github.com
```

```bash
# Apply from file (idempotent, creates new version if changed)
ant beta:agents apply -f agent.yaml

# Check current versions
ant beta:agents list
ant beta:agents versions list --agent-id agent_abc123

# Roll back to a previous version
ant beta:agents rollback --agent-id agent_abc123 --version 2
```

## Gotchas
- **`beta:` prefix is required** for all Managed Agents commands — `ant agents create` will fail; use `ant beta:agents create`
- **Auth token collision** — if both `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` are set in env, the API rejects the request; unset one before running `ant`
- **MCP credentials go in vaults, not system prompts** — use `ant beta:vaults credentials create` and pass `vault_ids` at session creation; hardcoding tokens in system prompts is a ToS violation and a security risk
- **Archive is permanent** — archiving an agent, environment, or session is irreversible; archived agents cannot be referenced by new sessions

learn.name: Google Antigravity 2.0
learn.oneLineDescription: Google's agent-first dev platform: desktop app + CLI + SDK powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash.

detail.whatItDoes:
Google Antigravity 2.0 is the agent-first development platform announced at Google I/O 2026 on May 19. It ships as three surfaces: a desktop application, a CLI (`antigravity` or `antg`), and a Go-based SDK. It replaces Gemini CLI as Google's primary developer tool and is powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash (289 tokens/sec output). The CLI component directly competes with Claude Code and Codex CLI.

Antigravity 2.0 adds subagent orchestration — spin up multiple specialized agents for complex workflows — with built-in cross-platform terminal sandboxing, credential masking, and hardened Git policies. The Antigravity SDK lets you embed Google's agentic capabilities in your own applications or self-host the agent harness on your own infrastructure. Managed Agents in the Gemini API (single API call spins up a fully sandboxed Linux agent) is also powered by the Antigravity harness.
detail.whoItsFor: Google Cloud developers and teams currently using Gemini CLI who need to migrate before the June 18, 2026 sunset. Developers who want a Claude Code alternative with Google account free-tier access and native Google Workspace, GCP, and Android Studio integration. Teams building Android apps who want AI-assisted migration from React Native or web frameworks.
pros: Powered by Gemini 3.5 Flash — outperforms Gemini 3.1 Pro at 4x the speed; no quality/cost tradeoff for Flash tier
Subagent orchestration built in — delegate subtasks to parallel specialized agents from a single session
Native Google Workspace and GCP integration (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive, Android Studio)
SDK enables self-hosted deployments for teams that need to keep data on-prem
cons: Replaces Gemini CLI — existing Gemini CLI installations and GEMINI.md configs need migration
New CLI syntax is different from Gemini CLI; muscle memory from `gemini` commands does not transfer
Desktop app currently requires Google AI Plus ($25/mo) or Ultra ($100/mo) for full agentic features; basic CLI is free
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+ or use the standalone binary
- A Google account (free tier available for CLI; Plus/Ultra for full agent features)
- macOS, Linux, or Windows

## Install the Antigravity CLI

```bash
# via npm (recommended, cross-platform)
npm install -g @google/antigravity

# verify
antg --version

# macOS Homebrew (once available in stable channel)
brew install google/antigravity/antg
```

## Authenticate

```bash
# Personal Google account (free tier)
antg login
# Opens browser — sign in with Google account

# Google AI Studio API key (higher limits)
export GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY="your-key"

# Vertex AI / GCP
gcloud auth application-default login
export GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT="your-project"
```

## First coding session

```bash
cd your-project

# Start interactive session (Gemini 3.5 Flash default)
antg

# Inside the session:
> Build a REST endpoint for user authentication in src/auth.ts
> Run the test suite and fix any failures
> Review this PR diff for security issues
```

## Subagent orchestration

```bash
# Spin up parallel specialized agents for a complex task
antg --orchestrate \
  --agents "security-reviewer,performance-analyzer,test-writer" \
  --task "Harden the payments module: security audit, perf profile, and 90% test coverage"
```

## Headless / CI mode

```bash
# Single-shot in CI
antg --headless -p "Review this diff for breaking API changes" < git.diff

# GitHub Actions
- name: API compat check
  run: git diff origin/main | antg --headless -p "List any breaking API changes"
  env:
    GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_AI_API_KEY }}
```

## Migrate from Gemini CLI

```bash
# Export existing GEMINI.md as ANTIGRAVITY.md (Antigravity reads both during transition)
cp GEMINI.md ANTIGRAVITY.md

# Migrate MCP server config
# Old: ~/.gemini/settings.json
# New: ~/.antigravity/settings.json (same JSON schema, different path)
cp ~/.gemini/settings.json ~/.antigravity/settings.json

# Verify MCP servers still work
antg mcp list
```

## Gotchas
- **Gemini CLI sunset is June 18, 2026** for individual/free-tier users — migrate now, not the day before
- **`GEMINI.md` is still read** by Antigravity during the transition period, but rename to `ANTIGRAVITY.md` for clarity; both files are read if present, with ANTIGRAVITY.md taking precedence
- **Subagent orchestration** requires Google AI Plus or Ultra subscription; single-agent mode is free
- **Desktop app and CLI share config** at `~/.antigravity/` — changing model settings in the desktop app affects CLI sessions immediately

learn.name: OpenAI Realtime 2 API
learn.oneLineDescription: Streaming speech-to-speech API with reasoning, translation, and transcription in one session.

detail.whatItDoes:
OpenAI's Realtime 2 API (released May 7, 2026) is a new family of speech-to-speech models that replace the deprecated Realtime API Beta. It ships three distinct surfaces in one API: Realtime 2 (full speech-to-speech with configurable reasoning), Realtime Translate (streaming speech-to-speech translation across languages), and Realtime Whisper (streaming speech-to-text transcription). All three use WebSocket or server-sent-event sessions for low-latency, streaming output.

The key upgrade over the beta is configurable reasoning — the model can spend tokens reasoning before producing audio, enabling more accurate responses for complex questions without a separate LLM hop. The old Realtime API Beta was removed from the API on May 12, 2026 simultaneously.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers building voice agents, real-time customer support bots, live translation tools, or meeting transcription products. Teams that were using the deprecated Realtime API Beta and need to migrate. Anyone who needs low-latency audio input and audio output from a single streaming API without stitching together separate STT, LLM, and TTS services.
pros: Three services (speech-to-speech, translation, transcription) in one unified API — no stitching
Configurable reasoning lets the model think before speaking, reducing hallucinations on complex queries
Streaming output keeps latency low even with reasoning enabled
Replaces the deprecated Realtime API Beta — existing WebSocket patterns mostly transfer with parameter updates
cons: Occasional audio quality issues noted in release notes: unexpected tone/pitch variations with certain voice options
Migration from Realtime API Beta is required — the beta endpoint was removed May 12, 2026 with no fallback
Reasoning mode increases token consumption; budget carefully for high-volume voice workloads
